body.statement: There are constants \(C_1,C_2<\infty\), depending only on \(s,M,v,\alpha\), such that if \(T_n\ge C_1\log(e/\kappa_n)\), then \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}\) is uniformly honest over \(\mathcal P_n\) and \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P[|I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}|]\le C_2\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}.\] Consequently \(L_n(\kappa_n)\asymp L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)\) in this region, uniformly over vanishing \(\kappa_n\). This strictly extends the fixed-jump oracle conclusion of Porter and Yu (2015) by allowing \(\kappa_n\to0\) down to the stated boundary and by delivering uniform honest connected-interval length.
body.justification: This theorem supplies an implementable honest procedure using only observable one-sided regressions and pins the region in which cutoff estimation is asymptotically costless for interval length.
body.gap: PorterYu2015 obtains oracle effect estimation after an unknown fixed jump, while NoackRothe2024 obtains weak-first-stage honesty at a known cutoff; neither result covers an unknown cutoff with \(\kappa_n\to0\).
body.consumer: Applied researchers obtain a data procedure that recovers the known-cutoff honest length once treatment uptake contains enough localization information.

obligation.what_is_open: A maximal inequality and localization-to-inversion argument with explicit constants for the scan--refine--invert rule, sufficient to prove uniform honesty and the claimed expected-length bound.
obligation.obstruction: The current construction names stages of a procedure but does not define a sample map: the grid, contrast weights, thresholds, bias radii, local-polynomial order, and test critical values are unspecified. Different choices change both the localization event and coverage, so the theorem cannot be proved for the named object from the frozen definition.
obligation.attempted: The natural bandwidth gives treatment signal-to-noise squared of order T_n and a union bound over translated locations costs order log(1/kappa_n). This recovers the theorem's regime at the level of orders, but it does not certify the particular interval or its uniform constants.
obligation.partial_result: At bandwidth \(h_n=(32\kappa_n/M)^{1/s}\), a treatment jump of order \(\kappa_n\) has per-location information of order \(n\kappa_n^2h_n=T_n\), while a grid of disjoint admissible locations has logarithmic size of order \(\log(1/\kappa_n)\).  This verifies the proposed signal-to-entropy scaling.  What is not yet proved is a uniform coverage and length theorem for the named rule because its construction does not specify the dyadic grid, contrast weights, selection thresholds, bias subtraction, local-polynomial order, or the acceptance critical value.
